According to all reports which come to my ears, our Fraternity is doing
is doing quite well. All 20,000-plus of us who have known the active undergraduate
experience have watched for progress

and we've seen it over the past few years.
There is no reason to believe that progress will not continue to be the watchword
from now on. It is in the cards. Two Chapters which departed during the difficult days
at many undergraduate institutions of higher learning during the late 1960's and early
1970's have been reactivated. Looking back over the years, we beheve that unsettled
period is not apt to appear again for a considerable time. Hence there is every
reason to

believe that we shall move ahead, and this movement may occur faster than we think.
What has been written would not have been put on paper were it not substantiated
not too many years back the Annual Giving
by facts worth considering. Think of it

Program raised a total of little more than $25,000. Last year it rose to over $63,000,
with more givers than ever. This progress is continuing during the 1979-80 period as
well. It has been reported that giving has exceeded the point reached last year at the
time of this writing, and 

more important

there are more brothers who have given
for the first time or who have given again after many years of not giving.
All of this bodes well for the regular operations of our Fraternity. It means that the
international office can function better and be of even more service to the Chapters.
Our two reactivated Chapters at the University of Wisconsin and at McGill University
in Montreal are still in need of special attention while working their way back into the
fold. There is a budding Chapter developing at Tufts, and the Nu Chapter at the
University of Toronto will soon be reactivated.
Should there ever be a question of why we need to expand the appeal of the Annual
Giving Program, perhaps these few examples may give us all a clue. The workload is
increasing. The demand is getting heavier. The cost of either or both is not going down.
So much for that. Now let's revert to the last issue of the Psi Upsilon Diamond,
wherein Owlie talked about the Endowment Fund. There is no need to refer to what
was therein contained except to state that real growth is not beyond the reach of us to

attain by 1983. For the last two years the international office has operated without a loss
for the first time since the idea of central administration was developed some years
back.
The Endowment Fund serves a very different purpose from the Annual Giving
Program. The Endowment Fund could provide the Fraternity with the wherewithal to
do all sorts of things which cannot be done at the present time. One million dollars,
properly invested, should produce more than $80,000 of income per year. Perhaps a
new Chapter has been established on some campus and now needs to acquire a better

or more suitable house. The Endowment Fund could provide all or part of the money

needed for that purpose. A sizable endowment also would permit the expenditure of
funds for the founding of Chapters on the campuses of many of our finest universities
where Psi Upsilon is not now represented.
Think about what you can do. Talk it over with your attorney, your banker, and your
wife. Then do what you would have wanted Psi Upsilon alumni to do when you were an
undergraduate of a Chapter. It is not difficult and, as the farmer said, "It gives a lot of
satisfaction."
